newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan growth in first-half 1996 very strong - govt.
newsitem.headline: Japan growth in first-half 1996 very strong - govt.

text.p: Japan's economic growth in the first half of this calendar year was very strong, chief government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama told a news conference on Friday.
The spokesman added that Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto would decide the timing of when to dissolve parliament after he visits the island of Okinawa on Tuesday, the spokesman said.

Commenting on the April-June gross domestic product (GDP) figures announced earlier, Kajiyama said the growth in the quarter was not necessarily weak as the growth in the preceding January-March period was very strong.
"When you look at the GDP growth in the first half of 1996, the economy was very strong," he said.
The government announced earlier in the day that Japan's gross domestic product rose a real 3.1 percent in the first half of calendar 1996 from the previous half-year period.
It said GDP fell a real 0.7 percent in the April-June quarter against the previous quarter. It had risen 2.9 percent over the same period in the previous quarter.
Kajiyama said Hashimoto would meet the two other leaders of the ruling coalition parties early next week to discuss the timing of a general election.
A regular meeting of the three leaders is scheduled on Thursday next week.
